- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above prior high.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.  
- In mean-reversion scenarios (price near 30-day moving average), model often holds too long; shorten forecast horizon or reduce slope of trend.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to adjust for delayed reaction.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.
